Prepare an LC-MS peak table for filtering

mc_prepare.Rd

Read a feature-by-sample peak table, identify intensity columns, and assign sample groups. Feature metadata are retained alongside the intensity values.

mc_prepare(data, type = c("mzmine", "generic", "xcms", "msdial"),
    sample_cols = NULL, sample_keywords = NULL, id_col = NULL,
    mz_col = NULL, rt_col = NULL, labels = NULL, token_sep = "_",
    token_index = 2)

Arguments

data

A local CSV filename or a data frame with one feature per row. Bundled files can be located with system.file(). For a web-hosted CSV, first read it with vroom::vroom(url, delim = ",") and pass the resulting table.

type

Input format: "mzmine" (default), "generic", "xcms", or "msdial". XCMS retention times are converted from seconds to minutes. Other formats require retention times in minutes. See compatible peak-table examples for the supported input layouts.

sample_cols

Intensity-column names or integer column positions after format conversion and column cleanup. Explicit selections take precedence over sample_keywords.

sample_keywords

Case-sensitive literal substrings used to identify intensity columns. A column is selected if its name contains at least one substring. If neither selector is supplied, columns with at least 70% finite numeric entries are considered, excluding identified feature columns and names beginning with row.

id_col

Feature-ID column name. If omitted, searches for row ID, Feature ID, or Alignment ID, then uses the first column. Original names recognized during format conversion may also be supplied.

mz_col

Feature m/z column name. Defaults to the standardized mz column; recognized original column names are accepted.

rt_col

Retention-time column name. Defaults to the standardized rt column; recognized original column names are accepted.

labels

One nonempty group label per sample. An unnamed vector must follow the selected sample columns; a named vector is matched to their names. If omitted, groups are extracted from sample names using token_sep and token_index.

token_sep

Literal separator used to split sample names when labels are omitted. Default: "_".

token_index

One-based position of the group name in each split sample name. Default: 2.

Details

Missing or nonnumeric intensity entries become zero. Values are not normalized or log-transformed. A unique internal identifier, .FID, is added to every feature; original IDs remain available for export. Explicit sample-column selection avoids accidentally treating numeric metadata as intensities.

Group labels can be replaced before filtering with mc_labels_from_metadata(), mc_labels_from_csv(), or mc_labels_from_names().

The object stores the current peak table rather than a second copy of the original table. Save the imported object if you want to compare alternative settings.

Value

A metabocensor_result list containing:

table

Current peak table, including metadata, sample intensities, and .FID.

sample_cols, labels

Intensity-column names and a named sample-group vector.

id_col, mz_col, rt_col

Selected identifier, m/z, and retention-time column names.

format

Column and format information needed to restore the input layout on export.

removed_ids, counts

Removed internal IDs and feature counts, populated by subsequent filtering.

See also

mc_labels_from_metadata, mc_filter_blank, mc_export

Examples

peak_file <- system.file(
  "extdata", "orbi_iimn_gnps_quant.csv",
  package = "MetaboCensoR", mustWork = TRUE
)
imported <- mc_prepare(
  peak_file, type = "mzmine",
  sample_keywords = c(".mzML", "Peak area")
)
metadata_file <- system.file(
  "extdata", "metadata.csv",
  package = "MetaboCensoR", mustWork = TRUE
)
imported$labels <- mc_labels_from_metadata(
  metadata_file, sample_names = imported$sample_cols,
  sample_col = "Sample name", label_col = "Label"
)
table(imported$labels)
